summary.title: Introduction to PyGame
summary.one_liner: Learn to set up a basic PyGame window, game clock, and quit-aware game loop in Python 3.
keywords: how to make a game in python
takeaways: Install PyGame with pip, then call pygame.init() before using any PyGame feature.
Create a display surface with pygame.display.set_mode((width, height)) and set a window title with set_caption.
Run a while loop that processes pygame.event.get() and exits on pygame.QUIT, then calls pygame.quit().
Use pygame.time.Clock() and clock.tick(60) to cap the frame rate; display.update() can refresh the whole screen or only parts of it.
summary.summary: This is the first lesson of a free Python 3 PyGame video game series on pythonprogramming.net, presented as a text page with embedded code snippets. It covers suggested prerequisites, installing PyGame with pip, and building a minimal game skeleton: initializing PyGame, creating an 800x600 display with a caption, setting up a clock, and writing a game loop that ends when the window is closed. The page also explains display.update versus display.flip and the role of frames per second. The rest of the page is a list of the series' later lessons, such as images, buttons, sounds, and packaging an executable.
